lesson_title: 1, 2, 4, ... What Comes Next? Three Right Answers
hook_text: 1, 2, 4, what comes next? If you said 8, you might be wrong. If you said 7, you might be right.
clip_script: 1, 2, 4. Next is 8, right? Doubling. But look at the differences: 1, then 2. If the differences keep growing by one, the next difference is 3 and the next term is 7. Both are real patterns. Three terms never decide. So here is the detective kit. Subtract neighbours: same every time, it is a taxi meter, step times n plus flag fall. Divide neighbours: same every time, chain message, a power. Differences growing steadily, by 2 every time? Squares in disguise — line the terms up against 1, 4, 9, 16 and read off the shift. Each term the two before added together? Rabbits — Fibonacci — and you must say where it starts. Get all the terms, run all the tests, then name the pattern.
visual_style: The numbers 1, 2, 4 on a whiteboard with a question mark that splits into two branches, one landing on 8 and one on 7; below, a four-item detective kit unrolls with icons for taxi, chain message, square dots and rabbits.
pacing: A quick trap, a beat of surprise, then four crisp tools.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never be fooled by three terms again.
